key_insight: Phase-controlled modal analysis separates gust-driven lift from evolving wake oscillations, revealing that near-zero total lift can mask substantial opposing modal contributions.
engineering_relevance: Separating transient gust loads from wake oscillations can improve interpretation of cylinder load responses and inform phase-aware flow-control strategies.
method: Simulate the same vortex gust at 64 cylinder-wake shedding phases at Re = 100.
Use POD to characterize wake departures and phase-controlled time-dependent DMD to track evolving modes, frequencies, and growth rates.
Integrate modal pressure and viscous stresses over the cylinder surface to resolve lift contributions.
evidence_signal: Across 64 phases, the zero-frequency mode carries most lift variation at gust arrival, while the fundamental conjugate pair dominates later oscillations; lift amplitude recovers but a phase shift persists.
watch_item: Findings are limited to the studied gust–cylinder interaction at Re = 100; applicability to turbulent wakes or other gust conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Phase-Controlled Time-Dependent Modal Analysis of Vortex-Gust Interaction with a Cylinder Wake
